quarterly_data.signal: CEO Michael Miebach / CFO Sachin Mehra (non-GAAP, currency-neutral): Q2 net revenue up 12%, above expectations; Payment Network net revenue +8% and Value-Added Services and Solutions net revenue +18% (security solutions, consumer acquisition and engagement, digital and authentication, business and market insights, pricing); operating expenses +10%; operating income +14%; net income +16%; EPS $5.04, up 19%.
quarterly_data.figure: net revenue +12%; Payment Network +8%; VAS +18%; operating income +14%; EPS $5.04

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Sachin Mehra, Q2 volumes (local currency): worldwide gross dollar volume +8%; U.S. +6% (credit +10%, debit +1%; 8% U.S. debit growth excluding the completed Capital One debit portfolio migration); outside the U.S. +9%; cross-border volume +12%; switched transactions +9%; contactless 80% of in-person switched purchase transactions; token penetration over 40% of switched transactions; card growth 5%, with 3.7 billion Mastercard and Maestro-branded cards issued globally. CEO: switching penetration 72%; commercial debit and credit volumes +12%; on average six million new small business cards added each quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: GDV +8%; cross-border +12%; switched transactions +9%; contactless 80%; 3.7 billion cards; switching penetration 72%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Sachin Mehra: domestic assessments +10%, cross-border assessments +20%, transaction processing assessments +12%, other network assessments $326 million; U.S. switched volume growth excluding Capital One debit was 10% (fuel and strong spending); cross-border card-not-present ex-travel +20%, helped by Venezuela (greater U.S. dollar availability; Mastercard is the market leader in that mainly debit market) and retail promotions; Middle East impacts moderated through Q2; first four weeks of July stable and strong; mass and affluent spending both holding up, affluent growing faster.
quarterly_data.figure: cross-border assessments +20%; other network assessments $326 million; cross-border card-not-present ex-travel +20%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Sachin Mehra, outlook (currency-neutral, excluding inorganic activity): Q3 net revenue growth at the high end of low double digits with about 0.5 ppt FX headwind and Q3 opex growth low double digits; full-year 2026 net revenue growth at the high end of low double digits - same range but now higher within it on the stronger first half - with about 1 ppt FX tailwind, full-year opex growth low double digits; non-GAAP tax rate 20%-21% for Q3 and Q4; Q3 rebates and incentives slightly higher as a share of payment network assessments than Q2; Middle East impact assumed at end-of-Q2 levels.
quarterly_data.figure: full-year net revenue growth high end of low double digits; tax rate 20%-21%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Michael Miebach / CFO Sachin Mehra: the BVNK acquisition (enterprise-grade payment orchestration, licensing and connectivity; Mastercard to serve as the trusted interoperable layer to send, receive, store and convert assets) is expected to close in Q3 2026, with minimal net revenue and some opex impact; OpenUSD, the open-standard stablecoin of a 140+ company consortium, is set to go live later this year and will be enabled on the Mastercard network alongside other coins (USDC, USDG today).
quarterly_data.figure: BVNK close expected Q3 2026; OpenUSD consortium 140+ companies

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Michael Miebach: in H1 2026 Mastercard won several hundred flips and deal expansions expected to drive trillions of dollars of incremental volume over the next decade - renewed JPMorgan Chase on Chase Freedom Flex (U.S.) and Banamex in Mexico (exclusivity for nearly all portfolios, almost 19 million cards); expanded Revolut (Ultra debit in Singapore and Australia, commercial in New Zealand); flipped Alliance Federal Credit Union's U.S. credit and debit and Eurobank's entire Greek portfolios (over 1 million new cards across the two); new Uber and Hilton co-brands in Mexico; exclusive across Saudi National Bank's portfolios; incremental issuance from Intuit; Truist chose its virtual card for corporate invoice payments; exclusive partnership with Riyadh Air; Mastercard Move partnerships with WeChat Pay Hong Kong and FlyRemit (India).
quarterly_data.figure: almost 19 million Banamex cards; over 1 million new cards (Alliance FCU and Eurobank)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Michael Miebach: the Central Bank of the UAE, through its subsidiary Al Etihad Payments, is partnering with Mastercard to build the switching technology for the UAE's next-phase domestic payments infrastructure; Mastercard will be the prime international scheme for credit cards co-badged with the domestic Jaywan scheme, will switch domestic debit and Jaywan-Mastercard co-badged credit transactions (incremental to its global switch) and will provide fraud prevention and cybersecurity services to the domestic switch.

CEO Michael Miebach: through an exclusive partnership with evermore, Mastercard is rolling out a program for U.S. food assistance beneficiaries (programs representing $100 billion of spend a year); the exclusive Alipay+ partnership is expanding in Mexico with Clip (a small and micro-business network approaching 1 million merchants; more than 70% of Mexican consumer payments are cash), with Mastercard exclusively tokenizing the stored wallet balances.
quarterly_data.figure: $100 billion annual U.S. food assistance spend; approaching 1 million merchants (Clip)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Michael Miebach, security services: seeing increased demand as AI and frontier models expand the threat landscape; Recorded Future intelligence brought to clients globally, with Wipro partnering to scale it; Mastercard Threat Intelligence identified more than 7 million card testing transactions across 192 countries in its first three quarters, preventing an estimated $172 million of fraud; Rogers Communications and Delivery Hero used Mastercard identity capabilities; Merchant Trust Services launched (AI-powered fraudulent-merchant detection). About 60% of VAS net revenue is network-linked; the Partner Advantage Program has more than 200 partners; services include portfolio conversions for Westpac and Yapi Kredi, cross-border marketing with Santander U.K. and portfolio optimisation for Bancolombia.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 7 million card testing transactions; $172 million fraud prevented; about 60% of VAS network-linked; more than 200 partners

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Michael Miebach, agentic commerce: Mastercard Agent Pay powers agentic transactions with tokenization and dispute resolution, including Verifiable Intent, innovated together with Google; Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines lets AI agents buy low-value digital services such as APIs, compute, data and content at machine speed (on-chain permissioning, off-chain settlement), with more than 30 industry participants at launch including Adyen, Ant International, BVNK, Checkout.com, Cloudflare, Coinbase and OKX; Mastercard calls itself the only network enabling machine-to-machine payments and expects cards to prevail in an agentic world ('it's early days').

CEO Michael Miebach: crypto co-brand volume more than tripled over the last two years, with relationships expanded with Bitget and Kraken this quarter; stablecoins have clear utility in some B2B and P2P flows but 'no problem to solve in P2M', and the company expects many coins and chains needing a trusted interoperable layer. Domestic switching: a real-time payment switch built in South Africa, and this kind of technology is being made available in Europe, where Mastercard partners with wallets such as Swish (Sweden) and Bizum (Spain).

CFO Sachin Mehra: European purchase volume growth was 16% in Q2 2024 on share wins (Santander, NatWest, UniCredit) and has slowed as those wins are lapped and as Mastercard passed on deals that did not make economic sense, such as Lloyds Credit, whose volumes are rolling off - 'volume for the sake of volume is not what this company should be chasing'.
quarterly_data.figure: 16% Europe purchase volume growth in Q2 2024
